instructions: Complete the notes below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
stem_block:
Testing four office layouts

Why firms pick the open-plan option
- Cheaper to build than an office cut up into (1) ........ rooms

The four layouts, each tried for a fortnight
- Plain open-plan, used as the point of comparison
- Zoned open-plan: rooms holding at most 40 staff, shut off by (2) ........ doors
- Activity-based: desks belonging to nobody, plus quiet rooms and shared areas
- Team office: semi-enclosed cubicles for four to six people, screened by sound-absorbing panels

How the layouts were judged
- Several separate (3) ........ of evidence were brought together
- Repeated staff surveys covering satisfaction, engagement, (4) ........ , energy, flow and how productive people felt
- Sensors reading noise, temperature, light and air; a count of technical output; watchers logging everyday habits at people's desks

What the sensors and the desks showed
- Noise in the plain open-plan room went over the recommended (5) ........ limits 20-30 per cent more often than in any rival design
- After a spell in that room, desk use in the next layout climbed by roughly 4 per cent - read as a real preference, not just a novelty effect

The authors' warning
- Results come from just one company, with a culture and (6) ........ of its own
- Other organisations should try the alternatives on their own staff

items.prompt: Why firms pick the open-plan option: Cheaper to build than an office cut up into (1) ........ rooms
items.evidence: Open-plan arrangements have nonetheless become the default choice for many growing companies, partly because they are cheaper to build and easier to reconfigure than offices divided into permanent rooms.
items.explanation: Paragraph A contrasts open-plan arrangements, which are cheaper to build, with offices divided into permanent rooms; the answer is therefore 'permanent'.

yeniden_uretim.eski_prompt: Why firms pick the open-plan option: Costs less to put up, and is simple to (1) ........ once needs change
yeniden_uretim.eski_kanit_cumlesi: Open-plan arrangements have nonetheless become the default choice for many growing companies, partly because they are cheaper to build and easier to reconfigure than offices divided into permanent rooms.
yeniden_uretim.neden_elendi: Bosluk 'easy/simple to ___ once needs change' kalibinin ucuna aciliyordu; kalip tek bir kavrami cagiriyor (yeniden duzenleme) ve E10 olcumunde model uc turun ucunde de dogru kavrami parcasiz verdi (rearrange / reconfigure). Acik plan ofisin ucuzluk disindaki ikinci gerekcesi kacinilmaz bicimde 'kolay yeniden duzenlenmesi' oldugu icin cerceve degisikligi kilidi acmiyordu.
yeniden_uretim.ne_degisti: Bosluk ayni cumlede kalip kaynagin kendi sectigi karsilastirma terimine kaydirildi: artik hedef, acik planin karsisina konan ofis turunu niteleyen sozcuk ('permanent'). Not satirindaki 'once needs change' ipucu kaldirildi, boylece kalicilik kavrami cerceveden cagrilmiyor. Parcasiz doldurma denemesinde 'separate / private / enclosed / individual' gibi rakipler ayni kaliba oturuyor ve dogru sozcugu vermiyor.

items.prompt: The four layouts: Zoned open-plan: rooms holding at most 40 staff, shut off by (2) ........ doors
items.evidence: Using a Latin square design, in which every team eventually experienced every condition but in a different order, the teams rotated through four distinct office layouts, each for a two-week period: a conventional open-plan office with minimal separation between desks, acting as the baseline; a zoned open-plan design with soundproof doors dividing spaces into rooms holding no more than 40 people; an activity-based design offering unassigned desks alongside dedicated focus rooms and collaboration areas; and a team-office design with large, partly enclosed cubicles seating four to six people behind sound-absorbing panels.
items.explanation: Paragraph B says that the zoned open-plan design is divided by soundproof doors into rooms holding no more than 40 people; since the question asks about the quality of the doors, the answer is 'soundproof'.

items.prompt: How the layouts were judged: Several separate (3) ........ of evidence were brought together
items.evidence: To evaluate the four designs, the researchers combined several sources of evidence.
items.explanation: Paragraph C says that to evaluate the four designs the researchers combined several sources of evidence; the answer is therefore 'sources'.

yeniden_uretim.eski_prompt: The four layouts: Team office: semi-enclosed cubicles for four to six people, screened by (3) ........ panels
yeniden_uretim.eski_kanit_cumlesi: Using a Latin square design, in which every team eventually experienced every condition but in a different order, the teams rotated through four distinct office layouts, each for a two-week period: a conventional open-plan office with minimal separation between desks, acting as the baseline; a zoned open-plan design with soundproof doors dividing spaces into rooms holding no more than 40 people; an activity-based design offering unassigned desks alongside dedicated focus rooms and collaboration areas; and a team-office design with large, partly enclosed cubicles seating four to six people behind sound-absorbing panels.
yeniden_uretim.neden_elendi: 2 ve 3 numarali yuvalarin ikisi de ayni kanit cumlesine (B/2) capaliydi; bir kanit cumlesinde en cok bir soru kurali bozuluyordu. B paragrafi iki cumleden olusuyor ve ilk cumle zaten true-false 8 numaraya ait, dolayisiyla iki yuvadan biri paragrafin disina cikmak zorundaydi. Not blogu pasaj sirasini izledigi icin tasinabilecek tek yer C paragrafinin ilk cumlesiydi.
yeniden_uretim.ne_degisti: Yuva C/1'e tasindi ve hedef, takim ofisinin panel turu yerine calismanin dort tasarimi nasil degerlendirdigi oldu. 'Sound-absorbing panels' bilgisi not blogunda bosluksuz olarak duruyor, yani ozetin icerigi korundu. Not: yeni yuva eskisinden daha kolay ('sources of evidence' yerlesik bir obek); butce kurali ile kalem gucu arasindaki bu takas raporda ayrica belirtildi.

items.prompt: How the layouts were judged: Repeated staff surveys covering satisfaction, engagement, (4) ........ , energy, flow and how productive people felt
items.evidence: Employees completed regular questionnaires measuring satisfaction, engagement, enjoyment, sense of energy, flow, and perceived productivity.
items.explanation: Paragraph C lists the things the regular questionnaires measured: satisfaction, engagement, enjoyment, sense of energy, flow and perceived productivity; the missing item is 'enjoyment'.

yeniden_uretim.eski_prompt: How the layouts were judged: Watchers logged everyday habits, for example how often people put on (4) ........
yeniden_uretim.eski_kanit_cumlesi: As an independent, behavioural proxy for technical output, the researchers also tracked the number of software code commits each team produced, and observers recorded how people actually used the different spaces, noting details such as how often employees wore headphones, retreated to quiet corners, or held impromptu conversations at their desks.
yeniden_uretim.neden_elendi: 'put on' fiili cikarilsa bile not, gurultu uzerine bir ofis calismasinda gozlemcilerin saydigi gunluk aliskanligi istiyor; bu cercevede 'headphones' pasajdan bagimsiz olarak akla gelen ilk ve neredeyse tek nesne. Kanit cumlesindeki oteki iki ornek (quiet corners, impromptu conversations) da ayni olcude tahmin edilebilir, yani hedefi cumle icinde kaydirmak da ise yaramiyor. E6 bu yuvayi ayni paragrafin olcum aracina (kod commit sayimi) tasimali.
yeniden_uretim.ne_degisti: Eski satir C/4'e capaliydi ve cevap ('headphones') gurultu uzerine bir ofis calismasinda akla gelen ilk nesneydi; ayni cumledeki oteki ornekler de (sessiz koseler, ayakustu sohbetler) ayni olcude tahmin edilebilirdi, yani hedefi cumle icinde kaydirmak ise yaramiyordu. Yeni satir C/4'e hic degmiyor: kanit C/2'ye, anketin olctugu alt boyutlarin listesine tasindi. ONE WORD ONLY sinirinda kalan tek pasaja ozgu aday buydu; kod commit sayimi da C/4 icinde oldugu icin kullanilamadi.

items.prompt: What the sensors and the desks showed: Noise in the plain open-plan room went over the recommended (5) ........ limits 20-30 per cent more often than in any rival design
items.evidence: Noise levels in the open-plan office exceeded recommended safe limits between 20 and 30 per cent more often than in any of the alternative designs.
items.explanation: Paragraph F says noise levels in the open-plan office exceeded recommended safe limits between 20 and 30 per cent more often than in any of the alternative designs; the answer is therefore 'safe'.

yeniden_uretim.eski_prompt: What people did rather than said: Read as a genuine preference, not merely a (5) ........ effect
yeniden_uretim.eski_kanit_cumlesi: Employees appeared to respond to this with their feet as well as their opinions: once a team's exposure to the open-plan condition ended, desk occupancy in whichever design followed it rose by about 4 per cent, a change the researchers interpreted as a behavioural preference for the newer arrangement rather than simply a novelty effect.
yeniden_uretim.neden_elendi: Bosluk 'merely a ___ effect' kalibinin icindeydi. E1 mekanizmayi 'belirsiz' isaretlemis, E5 ise bunun esdizim kilidine yakin durdugunu yazmisti: 'novelty effect' yerlesik bir esdizim, ama 'temporary / short-term / placebo' da ayni kaliba oturdugu icin dogru sozcugu tutturmak buyuk olcude sansa kaliyordu. Yani kalem hem sizintili hem de karari sansa birakan bir yuvaydi; iki savunulabilir cevap birakmamak icin yuva tasindi.
yeniden_uretim.ne_degisti: Kanit ayni pasajin F/2 cumlesine tasindi ve bosluk artik calismanin kendi olctugu esige aciliyor (gurultunun asdigi 'recommended safe limits'). Rakip doldurmalar ('noise / legal / maximum / decibel') cerceveye oturuyor ama pasajin kullandigi sozcuk degil, dolayisiyla karar F/2'yi okumaya bagli. 'Novelty effect' ifadesi not blogunda bosluksuz olarak duruyor, yani ozetin anlami korundu.

items.prompt: The authors' warning: Results come from just one company, with a culture and (6) ........ of its own
items.evidence: They caution, though, that the findings come from a single technology company with its own particular culture and workflows, and that organisations considering a similar redesign would do well to test alternatives with their own staff rather than assume the same ranking will hold everywhere.
items.explanation: Paragraph H warns that the findings come from a single technology company with its own particular culture and workflows; since 'culture' is already given, the word that fills the gap is 'workflows'.
